title: Steady state of a cold-plate network
prompt:
A liquid-cooled server has two GPUs on one cold plate. Model it as a thermal network: nodes (GPU junctions, cases, the plate) joined by thermal conductances, with the plate cooled by coolant held at a fixed temperature.

Write `steady_state(links, q, t_coolant)`. Each row of `links` is `(i, j, g)`: a conductance of `g` W/K between nodes `i` and `j`, where `j = -1` means the link goes to the coolant. `q[i]` is the heat generated at node `i`, in W. Return the node temperatures `T` in °C.

At steady state the heat leaving each node through its links equals the heat generated there: Σ g·(Tᵢ − Tⱼ) = qᵢ, summed over node i's links. Assemble the matrix that says this for every node (it's built exactly like a stiffness matrix in structural analysis), then solve it. Raise `ValueError` if the temperatures aren't determined because the matrix is singular. Don't compute an inverse.
hints: Write the balance for one node by hand: a node with links to nodes j and k has (g_ij + g_ik)·Tᵢ − g_ij·Tⱼ − g_ik·Tₖ = qᵢ. Where does each g land in the matrix?

Each link (i, j, g) adds g to K[i, i] and K[j, j] and subtracts g from K[i, j] and K[j, i]. A link to the coolant adds g to K[i, i] only; its known temperature moves to the right-hand side as g·t_coolant. If some group of nodes has no path to the coolant, adding a constant to all of their temperatures changes nothing, so K is singular: check its rank before solving.

K = np.zeros((n, n)); rhs = q.astype(float).copy(). For i, j, g in links (cast i and j to int): K[i, i] += g; if j < 0: rhs[i] += g * t_coolant; else: K[j, j] += g; K[i, j] -= g; K[j, i] -= g. Then raise if np.linalg.matrix_rank(K) < n, and return np.linalg.solve(K, rhs).

misconceptions.solve-not-inverse: To solve Ax = b, call np.linalg.solve(A, b). Forming inv(A) costs more and gives residuals that can be orders of magnitude larger.
misconceptions.singular-floating-network: A network with no path to a fixed temperature is like a structure with no supports: a rigid-body (uniform) shift is in the null space, so the matrix is singular and the solution isn't determined.
